round1.evidence: AddFilesToWorkIntent.swift:178–197 snapshots every input before deriving identity and passes snapshot URLs to publication. At :389–400, each successfully written chunk is the chunk hashed; captureIdentity at :292 performs no file I/O. Read/write failures throw before publication. WorkCaptureFileCaptureTests.swift:303–350 rewrites the external source after identity calculation and asserts that the claimed payload remains 'alpha', while a subsequent snapshot of 'bravo' produces a different ID. Publishing the original source in that scenario would fail the payload assertion. The test exercises the helpers and publisher directly, rather than perform().

AppDelegate.swift:280 and :450 invoke the application-lifetime hook. Its pending guard at :315 precedes activation and reveal at :319–320; an ordinary launch therefore does neither. The reveal reaches ConduckApp.swift:305–309, which opens main. Consumption remains behind the composer and active-destination guards in WorkboardCaptureCanvas.swift:218–222. A read-only reproduction of the new source guard passed against HEAD and failed against 5c401df, where both lifecycle calls and the hook are absent. Actual AppKit cold-launch timing was not exercised.

findings.title: Snapshot copying has no enforced byte limit
findings.claim: A source enlarged after preflight is copied completely before its measured size is refused. The new snapshot stage can therefore consume arbitrarily more disk than the documented approximately 1 GB peak.
findings.evidence: perform() checks declared sizes at :170, snapshots the entire set at :178–186, and checks measured sizes only at :191. snapshot() reads until EOF and writes every chunk at :389–400 without checking maximumFileBytes or the remaining envelope budget. Before this fix, identity calculation only read the source; WorkCaptureInbox.swift:1122 then remeasured it through refuseOversizedSources before copying. The existing size tests exercise the inbox directly and bypass the newly introduced snapshot stage.
findings.scenario: Preflight observes a small video. Before snapshot() opens it, an editor or file provider replaces it with a multi-gigabyte version. The shortcut writes the replacement into scratch until EOF or disk exhaustion, despite the 256 MB per-file ceiling. With sufficient space it eventually reports fileTooLarge; without it, it consumes the available space and reports unreadableFile.
findings.fix: Enforce the per-file ceiling and remaining aggregate budget before each snapshot write. Abort and reclaim staging immediately when either would be exceeded. Add a regression where the source grows after its declared size is captured.
findings.refutationAttempt: The second refusal prevents oversized publication, but runs after the disk consumption. The defer cleans up an ordinary failure, and the recognized scratch prefix allows later sweeping after process death; neither limits peak usage. Fixed-size reads bound memory, not bytes written.
